incident-bot: PagerDuty alert: service=private-control-plane | customer=Acme Corp | region=us-west-2 | symptom=control-plane-unreachable | severity=P1
pagerduty: Incident ACME-PRIVATE-CTRLPLANE triggered at 2026-03-14T01:33:09Z — https://pagerduty.example/INC123456 (page sent to: oncall)
sanjay: ack'd — I'm oncall for infra, joining. Paging network and platform.
emma: on it. checking agent heartbeats and LB health now. first glance: control-plane LB shows 502/504 surge starting ~01:30Z.
priya: seeing agent heartbeats drop for customer-acme in our telemetry: last heartbeat 01:29:47Z from their on-prem agent.
matt: I can reproduce curl failure to health endpoint through the transit gw: `curl -v https://acme-ctrl.example/api/health` -> `504 Gateway Time-out`.
priya: quick logs from the agent stream (truncated):
```
[01:28:51Z] INFO heartbeat sent
[01:29:47Z] WARN tls handshake timeout
[01:30:12Z] ERROR connection reset by peer
[01:30:30Z] INFO agent shutting down (graceful?)
```
emma: checking VPC route tables and TGW attachments. No route flaps showing from our control plane side. Querying transit gw flow logs.
priya: can we confirm customer-edge? Nora, any updates from CS (you pinged Acme)?
nora-cs: Acme says they didn't change anything on their side, their ops reported VPN flapped around 01:29Z and their BGP session briefly went down for ~40s. They opened a ticket with their network team.
sanjay: good to know. tagging network: @emma please escalate BGP/TGW. Also let's prepare mitigation plan: 1) try restarting redwood-agent on customer proxy via management channel (if we have rights), 2) if agent restart fails, failover customer to public-proxy fallback route, 3) keep customer informed.
emma: on the TGW side, I see a flood of retransmits from the customer's IP to the control plane LB IP at 01:29:xx. Packets show MSS/MTU mismatch on capture. Might be path MTU blackhole after a recent MTU change on their edge device.
matt: try a probing command from a jump-host: `tcptraceroute -m 30 -s <our-ip> <acme-edge-ip>` — I'm running now.
priya: I'm attempting a remote restart of the agent via our management plane: `ssh acme-gw 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent'` (using existing access token).
priya: ssh returned: `Connection timed out`. management channel also shows no response — suggests the control plane can't reach their management IP.
emma: network team (cc @matt) recommends asking Acme to restart their edge device BGP or revert MTU change; nudge them to check if jumbo frames were enabled for an internal window.
nora-cs: pinged Acme ops: they're booting their edge device now. ETA ~10m. They've requested a temporary workaround from us if possible. They also reported customers seeing console 504s for admin panel and some API timeouts.
sanjay: mitigation step: enable fallback proxy route for Acme to route control plane calls over our public proxy cluster (policy: temporary, authenticated). Priya, can you flip the routing policy? This will add cost but reduce customer impact.
priya: I've prepared the policy patch. applying now:
```
PATCH /routing/policies/acme
{"fallback": "public-proxy-us-west-2", "ttl": 900}
```
priya: patch applied. routing change propagated to edge routers (2 of 3), waiting for full convergence.
matt: I see traffic start to flow through public-proxy at 01:48Z, health checks to control plane return 200 from those probes.
nora-cs: Acme reports admin console is partially back — some pages still 504 but core API endpoints look healthier. They're appreciative of the quick mitigation. :heart:
emma: still investigating root cause for BGP flap; TGW logs show PMTU blackhole followed by flapping sessions. network team requested packet capture from Acme edge once they're up.
sanjay: escalation: if Acme edge doesn't stabilize within 30m, we escalate to oncall-eng-leads for potential manual reroute and longer-term remediation (SRE + Network + Customer). Notifying @matt-lead.
priya: rechecking agent heartbeat: new heartbeats appearing at 01:58Z after the customer's edge boot. agent shows `Connected` and `version=1.12.3`.
matt: running health check sweep: all control plane routes for Acme now stable. no 5xx spikes in last 5m.
nora-cs: Acme confirms degraded experience resolved for most customers, they will keep monitoring. They've asked for a postmortem and timeline.
emma: preliminary incident summary for postmortem: cause = transient BGP session flap due to MTU change at customer edge causing PMTU issues and stalled TLS handshakes; effect = agent heartbeats dropped, control plane calls timed out, customer console 504s. mitigation = customer edge reboot + temporary routing fallback to public-proxy + agent restart.
sanjay: handing off follow-up and postmortem to Emma (incident lead) and Priya (mitigation runbook updates). I'll remain available for escalation. Next oncall (emma) acknowledged handoff at 02:05Z.
priya: action item: add automatic detection for repeated TLS handshake timeouts + auto-fallback to public-proxy for private deployments to reduce MTTR. Filing a ticket: INFRA-3421.
matt: closing the PagerDuty incident page and marking as mitigated. Will add timeline and logs to postmortem doc.
incident-bot: Incident ACME-PRIVATE-CTRLPLANE status changed to MITIGATED at 2026-03-14T02:12:01Z — responder: matt
sanjay: thanks team. followups logged, postmortem owners assigned. :thumbsup:
nora-cs: sending customer heartbeat and timeline. Acme says thanks to the rapid response.
priya: final note — keep this in ops runbook for Private: verify MTU/BGP stability after customer network changes; add checklist item when onboarding private customers.
emma: I'll draft the postmortem and include packet captures and TGW logs. target publish 2026-03-15.
matt: resolved — moving thread to incident archive.
